title: Power Automate: self-healing repairs desktop flow selector failures with AI
summary: Hold: the current Microsoft documentation names GPT-6 Luna, captures the parent window rather than the full desktop, and now exposes self-healing details in portal action logs. The briefing also retains unsupported Anthropic prerequisites and two admin paths whose cited self-healing page no longer documents those controls.

claims.claim: Self-healing is an AI fallback for missing or changed UI elements in desktop UI and browser automation.
claims.quote: Self-healing (preview) in Power Automate for desktop is an AI-powered capability that helps desktop flows recover from UI and browser automation failures caused by missing or changed UI elements.

claims.claim: When an existing selector no longer locates the intended UI element, AI identifies the element and generates an alternative selector.
claims.quote: When an existing selector can no longer locate the intended UI element, Power Automate for desktop uses AI to identify the element and generate an alternative selector.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes self-healing as an agentic feature improving desktop flow resilience.
claims.quote: Self-healing is an agentic feature that improves the resilience of desktop flows by recovering from UI or web automation failures.

claims.claim: The roadmap preview includes action-level opt-in for automatic recovery attempts.
claims.quote: The preview phase includes an action-level opt-in option for automatically trying to recover from a selector error

claims.claim: The roadmap plans an additional flow-level opt-in at general availability.
claims.quote: the GA phase will additionally include a flow-level opt-in option

claims.claim: Self-healing is user-opt-in, enabled by makers per action rather than changing existing flows automatically.
claims.quote: Enable self-healing per action: ... Turn on Self-healing (Preview). Searched: "self-healing" administrator tenant environment switch API enable action; no separate self-healing admin switch found.

claims.claim: Makers enable self-healing in Power Automate for desktop through action > Error handling > Self-healing (Preview).
claims.quote: Select a supported UI or browser automation action in the flow designer. ... Open the Error handling settings. ... Turn on Self-healing (Preview).

claims.claim: The cited self-healing page documents Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Anthropic.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center and select Copilot > Settings > View all. ... Select AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors. ... select Anthropic, and Save.
claims.fix: If retained as a general provider control, set the path to 'Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Anthropic' and docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/connect-to-ai-subprocessor. The current self-healing docs URL shows neither this control nor its last steps; do not present it as a self-healing prerequisite.

claims.claim: The cited self-healing page documents Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Platform > External models > Anthropic.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments, and then select the environment. ... select Settings. ... select Product > Features. ... turn each applicable model provider setting On or Off.
claims.fix: If retained as a general provider control, replace the path with 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Anthropic' and docs with https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/allow-llm-generative-responses. The current self-healing docs URL shows neither the control nor its last steps; remove its presentation as a self-healing prerequisite.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environment groups > environment group > Add rules > Power Platform Anthropic reaches the group rule.
claims.quote: select Environment groups, and then select the environment group. ... Select the Add rules tab. ... Select the checkbox ... Power Platform Anthropic ... Select each rule to see its details page, confirm or configure its feature settings
claims.fix: The path reaches rule selection but stops before configuration. Add to the existing note: 'Select the rule, configure its feature settings, then select Save, Add and Apply changes.'

claims.claim: Cross-region data movement is set in Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Generative AI features > Edit > Move data across regions.
claims.quote: Manage > Environments. Select your environment ... In the Generative AI features card, select Edit. ... select the Move data across regions checkbox.

claims.claim: Set-PowerPlatformGenerativeAiSettings -EnvironmentName <environment-id> -CrossGeoDataMovement $true enables cross-region data movement.
claims.quote: Set-PowerPlatformGenerativeAiSettings -EnvironmentName 00aa00aa-bb11-cc22-dd33-44ee44ee44ee -CrossGeoDataMovement $true -BingSearch $true -Microsoft365Services $true ... Sets the generative AI settings allowing for cross-geography data movement

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Automate > Copilot in Power Automate > On enables Copilot in Power Automate.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Settings. Under the Power Automate section, select Copilot in Power Automate, then enable the On check box in the displayed pane.
